learning_outcomes.text: Understand the regulations involved in the calculation of concrete structures (CTE and Structural Code), both regarding actions and their combination, as well as the design and verification of sections and structural regions.
Master the specific terminology used at a professional level.
Learn the most important characteristics of concrete and reinforcing steel.
Master the calculation of reinforced concrete sections in Ultimate Limit State for normal and tangential stresses.
Know and apply the necessary checks in the different Service Limit States.
Study constructive options for the execution of industrial buildings (walls, foundations...).
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing within their field of application
Ability to search for and manage information
Possess the ability to make decisions
Develop critical reasoning
Develop interpersonal skills
Develop the ability to work in a team
Ability to work in an international context
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team
Acquire commitment to ethics and social responsibility
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity)
Ability to work autonomously
Show initiative and entrepreneurial spirit
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement
Be sensitive to environmental issues
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions
Applied knowledge of metal structures and reinforced concrete

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacture, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes
Ability to direct activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section
Ability to carry out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions
Ability to exercise teaching in the terms required by current regulations

syllabus_topics: Reinforced Concrete Structures: combination of actions and safety factors
Reinforced Concrete Structures: Ultimate Limit States. Normal Stresses. Tangential Shear Stresses.
Reinforced Concrete Structures: Service Limit States. Cracking. Deformation.
Reinforced Concrete Structures: Structural regions. Strut-and-tie method. Short corbels.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous practical monitoring: written tests and autonomous development exercises.

assessment_rules: The final grade is the weighted average of all procedures, and the course is passed with a grade above 5 in this average. For the second call, only blocks with a grade below 4 must be re-evaluated. An autonomous development assignment, if established, must be submitted with a grade above 4 to pass. Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a zero grade for that component.
